why: SEAL's editors show that the Old Babylonian copies read kītam, a reed mat, which the next line confirms with "laying the bed." They explain the Nineveh scribe's ke-e-šá as a misreading of an older ki-ta, modernized, not the city of Kesh. Older editions (Lambert and Millard 1969; Foster) read the verb as "praise" and the noun as Kesh.
